chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Amr ibn Shimir, from al-Fadl, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Surely an angel descends with a scroll at the beginning of the day and the beginning of the night, and writes therein the deeds of the son of Adam. So do good at its beginning and do good at its end, for indeed Allah will forgive you for what is between that, if Allah wills.'
For indeed Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, says: 'So remember Me; I will remember you.' And He says: 'And certainly the remembrance of Allah is the greatest.'

key_terms.عَمَلَ ابْنِ آدَمَ: Deeds of the son of Adam (humanity)
key_terms.فَاذْکُرُونِی أَذْکُرْکُمْ: So remember Me, I will remember you
key_terms.لَذِکْرُ اللَّهِ أَکْبَرُ: And certainly the remembrance of Allah is the greatest

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of performing good deeds at the beginning and end of the day according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, the Prophet (s.a.w.s.) highlights the spiritual significance of the day's transitions, where angels record deeds, urging believers to anchor their routine with righteous acts to secure divine forgiveness. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (awareness of God) and the belief that consistent, small good deeds at key moments carry immense weight in the divine ledger.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam  Muhammad  Baqir  (a.s.)  narrates  that  the  Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “Surely an angel descends carrying a scroll in the beginning of day and night and writes the deeds of men. Hence one should do good deeds in the beginning of day and night. God willing, you will be forgiven during the other times also if Allah wills, because Allah, the Mighty and   Sublime   says:   ‘Therefore   remember   Me,   I   will remember   you’. And   He   says:   ‘and   certainly   the remembrance of Allah is the greatest’.”
